uncertainty_note: The flow description alone does not confirm absence of such controls; this is a compliance risk inferred from the workflow.

title: Video stream may disclose more granular personal data than necessary
description: Streaming full approved video to the child may disclose fine-grained personal data embedded in the content or stream metadata beyond what is strictly necessary to provide the viewing function, such as precise visual/audio details or rich metadata.
assumptions: Assumes the approved video or its delivery metadata can contain personal data about the child or others appearing in or associated with the content.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify the exact video content or metadata, so the presence of personal data is plausible but not certain.

title: Video delivery traffic can reveal when the child is watching content
description: Observation of the stream from the Video Management Service to the Child User can allow an observer to detect that the child is currently receiving approved video, revealing activity patterns or presence.
assumptions: Assumes an attacker or third party can observe network communications or traffic characteristics associated with the stream.
uncertainty_note: This is a generic communication-observation risk; the description does not state whether transport protections or traffic-hiding measures exist.

title: Child may be unaware of personal data processing involved in video streaming
description: The child data subject may not be aware that streaming approved video can involve processing of personal data, such as viewing activity, device/network metadata, or identifiers associated with content delivery.
assumptions: Assumes the child is a data subject for at least some metadata generated or processed during streaming.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not explicitly mention notices, explanations, or UI cues, so this remains a plausible but unconfirmed threat.

title: Streaming may violate data minimization if unnecessary personal data is included
description: If the video stream or associated delivery metadata includes more personal data than needed to provide approved video to the child, the processing on this flow may conflict with the data minimization principle.
assumptions: Assumes personal data is present in the stream payload or metadata and that some of it is not necessary for delivery.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on implementation details and jurisdictional applicability, which are not provided.

title: Browsing-history profiling enables linkage of child records
description: The childprofiles collection contains child browsing data that is sent to the AI recommendation engine. Browsing behavior is inherently suitable for profiling, allowing records and events belonging to the same child to be linked over time and across interactions.
assumptions: Assumes the childprofiles collection stores per-child browsing histories or behavior traces rather than only fully aggregated statistics.

title: Child browsing data may identify a child through quasi-identifiers
description: Even if direct identifiers are absent, browsing data can contain combinations of attributes, interests, timestamps, and behavioral patterns that make a child identifiable or distinguishable when processed by the AI engine.
assumptions: Assumes the transferred browsing data includes sufficiently granular events or attributes to single out a child profile.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify exact fields, so identifiability is inferred from typical browsing-profile content.

title: Browsing records can serve as attributable evidence about a child’s actions
description: The transferred browsing data may act as evidence that a particular child profile viewed or interacted with certain content, reducing deniability regarding those actions or interests.
assumptions: Assumes records are associated with a persistent child profile or account reference.
uncertainty_note: It is unclear whether the profile is directly tied to a real-world identity or only to an internal child account.

title: AI analysis may involve unnecessary enrichment of child browsing data
description: Sending child browsing data into an AI recommendation engine introduces further analysis, inference, and enrichment beyond mere storage. If the engine derives additional traits, preferences, or sensitive inferences not strictly necessary for recommendations, this creates unnecessary processing and disclosure risk.
assumptions: Assumes the recommendation engine performs behavioral analysis or inference rather than simple rule-based matching.
uncertainty_note: The flow is marked planned, so the exact scope of AI processing is not yet confirmed.

title: Children or guardians may be unaware that browsing data is used for AI recommendations
description: The planned transfer of child browsing data from storage to an AI recommendation engine may not be apparent to the child data subject or their guardian, creating unawareness about downstream profiling and recommendation processing.
assumptions: Assumes this AI use is not clearly communicated in notices or interfaces.
uncertainty_note: No transparency or notice mechanisms are described, so this is a plausible but not confirmed threat.

title: Planned AI recommendation processing of child browsing data may lack a valid lawful basis or trigger child-data compliance issues
description: Using child browsing data in an AI recommendation engine can raise GDPR compliance concerns, especially if profiling, automated decision-making, or child-specific protections are not properly addressed. The planned nature of the flow suggests lawfulness and safeguards may not yet be established.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to GDPR or similar child-data protection obligations.
uncertainty_note: Jurisdiction, lawful basis, and whether recommendations constitute regulated automated decision-making are not specified.

title: Browsing data enables advertiser-side profiling and linkage
description: The AI Recommendation Engine sends browsing data to third-party advertisers. Even without explicit names, browsing behavior can be analyzed to build or match profiles, allowing the advertiser to link this flow to an individual or an existing advertising profile.

title: Advertisers can link browsing records using quasi-identifiers
description: At the advertiser destination, combinations of browsing events, interests, timing, and context may act as quasi-identifiers that allow records from this flow to be linked to the same person across sessions or datasets.
uncertainty_note: The exact fields in 'browsing data' are not specified, so this assumes the shared data contains enough behavioral/contextual detail to support linkage.

title: Browsing data may contain revealing attributes that support identification
description: Browsing data commonly contains revealing attributes such as viewed content, interests, timestamps, device or session context, and behavioral patterns. Sharing such data with advertisers can make the data subject identifiable or easier to identify.

title: Advertisers may identify users from combinations of shared browsing attributes
description: At the advertiser side, combinations of shared browsing attributes can function as quasi-identifiers, enabling identification or singling out of a user when combined with the advertiser's existing datasets.
uncertainty_note: Identification risk depends on the granularity of the browsing data and what auxiliary data the advertiser already holds.

title: Shared browsing records can become attributable evidence of user behavior
description: Sending browsing data to advertisers creates records that may later be used to attribute specific browsing actions or interests to a person, reducing plausible deniability regarding what content was viewed or interacted with.
uncertainty_note: This assumes the browsing data is associated with a stable account, device, cookie, or other persistent context at some point in processing.

title: Advertisers can detect user activity through observed browsing-data transmissions
description: The transmission of browsing data to third-party advertisers allows those advertisers to observe when user activity occurs and infer engagement, interests, or presence based on the communications they receive.

title: Propagation of browsing data to third-party advertisers may be unnecessary
description: This flow propagates personal browsing data from the recommendation engine to an external advertising party. Based on the description, this appears to extend access beyond the core recommendation function and may disclose data where it is not strictly needed for the original service functionality.

title: Browsing data is disclosed to predetermined external parties
description: Third-party advertisers are external recipients of browsing data. Making this data accessible to such predetermined outside parties increases exposure and creates a disclosure risk beyond internal processing.

title: Users may be unaware that browsing data is shared with advertisers
description: The flow description indicates planned sharing of browsing data to advertisers. Data subjects may not reasonably expect their browsing behavior within the service to be disclosed to third-party advertisers, creating unawareness of processing.
uncertainty_note: Whether users are actually unaware depends on the service's notices and UX, which are not provided.

title: Users may lack meaningful control over advertiser sharing preferences
description: If browsing data is sent to advertisers as planned, data subjects may lack the ability to opt in, opt out, or otherwise control this disclosure and related downstream processing.
uncertainty_note: The existence of consent or privacy controls is not specified, so this is a risk inferred from the planned third-party sharing.

title: Planned advertiser sharing may rely on invalid or absent consent
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may require valid, specific, informed consent depending on the legal basis and jurisdiction. If such consent is absent, bundled, or not freely given, the processing may be unlawful.
uncertainty_note: This is a compliance risk inference only; the lawful basis, jurisdiction, and consent design are not provided.

title: Advertiser sharing risks violating data minimization
description: Sending browsing data from the recommendation engine to advertisers may process more personal data than necessary for the stated recommendation functionality, creating a data minimization compliance risk.

title: Government ID image storage enables strong record linkage
description: Storing government ID images creates a highly unique identifier that can link this record to the same individual across sessions, accounts, or related datasets. The image itself and any visible document number or personal details can serve as strong linkage keys.

title: Stored government ID images directly identify the data subject
description: Government ID images typically contain directly identifying information such as full name, photograph, date of birth, document number, and address. Persisting these images in the file system means identified data is being processed and stored.

title: Government ID images can serve as attributable evidence
description: A stored government ID image can be used to attribute the record to a specific person and support claims about that person's identity or participation in an onboarding or authentication process, reducing deniability.

title: Highly sensitive identity documents are stored
description: Government ID images are a highly sensitive personal data type. Storing full images may disclose more sensitive personal data than functionally necessary if the purpose could be achieved with less intrusive verification outputs or extracted attributes.
uncertainty_note: The flow description says the images are stored, but it does not state whether retaining full images is strictly necessary for the authentication purpose.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that ID images are retained in backend storage
description: The flow indicates storage of government ID images in a backend file system. If users are not clearly informed that their identity documents are retained after upload, they may be unaware of the storage and subsequent processing of highly sensitive personal data.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the system provides clear notice about storage and retention; that context is not given.

title: Potential data minimization non-compliance from storing full ID images
description: Persisting full government ID images may exceed what is necessary for the stated authentication purpose if verification could be completed without long-term storage of the complete document image. This creates a potential violation of the data minimization principle.
uncertainty_note: Potential rather than certain non-compliance, because the lawful and functional necessity for storing full images is not specified.

title: JWT in localStorage enables linking via stable unique identifier
description: A JWT commonly contains a stable subject, account identifier, or other unique claims. Storing it in browser localStorage allows data associated with that token to be linked to the same user across sessions within the browser context.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains stable unique claims such as sub, user id, email, or equivalent account reference.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not list JWT claims explicitly; applicability depends on whether the token payload includes a stable identifier, which is common but not guaranteed.

title: JWT stored in localStorage may contain identifier enabling identification
description: If the JWT payload is readable client-side and includes claims such as subject, email, username, or tenant-specific account id, the stored token contains a unique reference that can identify or single out the data subject.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is not encrypted and includes identifying or pseudonymous claims, as is typical for bearer JWTs.
uncertainty_note: JWTs are often only signed, not encrypted, but the exact token format and claims are not provided.

title: Stored JWT can serve as attributable evidence of user session or actions
description: A JWT tied to a specific account and retained in localStorage can later be used to attribute a session or related requests to a particular user, reducing deniability regarding use of the application from that browser context.
assumptions: Assumes downstream requests use this JWT for authenticated actions and that the token is bound to a user account.
uncertainty_note: This is indirect for this flow alone because attribution depends on later use of the token in authenticated requests.

title: JWT retention in localStorage may exceed functional necessity
description: localStorage persists until explicitly cleared, so storing an authentication JWT there can keep personal or account-linked data longer than needed for the active session. This increases disclosure risk if the browser is later accessed or compromised.
assumptions: Assumes the token persists beyond the immediate authenticated session and is not promptly removed on logout or expiry.
uncertainty_note: The actual token lifecycle and cleanup behavior are not described, but persistence is inherent to localStorage.

title: JWT encoding may disclose more personal data than needed
description: JWTs often encode multiple claims in a client-readable format. Storing the full token in localStorage may expose additional personal data or metadata embedded in the token beyond what is strictly needed merely to maintain session state.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains multiple readable claims rather than only an opaque reference.
uncertainty_note: The exact JWT contents are unknown; some deployments use minimal claims while others include profile or authorization data.

title: User may be unaware that authentication token is persistently stored in localStorage
description: Persistently storing a JWT in browser localStorage may not be visible or understandable to the data subject. The user may not realize that account-linked authentication data remains on the device after the session ends or browser closes.
assumptions: Assumes the application does not clearly inform users about this storage behavior.
uncertainty_note: Awareness depends on the application's notices and UX, which are not provided.

title: User may lack effective control to erase persisted JWT from localStorage
description: If the application stores the JWT in localStorage without providing clear logout, revoke, or delete mechanisms, the user may lack practical ability to remove the persisted authentication data from the browser.
assumptions: Assumes no robust in-app mechanism exists to clear localStorage and invalidate the token.
uncertainty_note: The presence of logout, token revocation, or storage-clearing controls is not specified.

title: Persistent JWT storage may violate storage limitation expectations
description: Because localStorage is persistent by default, storing an account-linked JWT there risks retaining personal data longer than necessary for the authentication purpose, creating potential non-compliance with storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT qualifies as personal data because it identifies or is linkable to a user, and that retention is not tightly bounded and enforced.
uncertainty_note: Legal applicability depends on jurisdiction and implementation details such as expiry, logout handling, and token contents.

title: Storing JWT in localStorage indicates insufficient privacy-aware cybersecurity risk management
description: Persisting bearer tokens in localStorage increases exposure to client-side compromise scenarios and associated privacy harm if account-linked token contents are accessed. This can indicate insufficient cybersecurity risk management where privacy risks of token storage choices are not adequately addressed.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is a bearer token and compromise of browser storage would expose account-linked data or enable access to it.
uncertainty_note: This is grounded in common security/privacy practice concerns around localStorage, but the prompt provides no explicit attacker model.

title: Child history enables linkage and profiling by the parent
description: The child history retrieved for parent review may contain longitudinal events, behaviors, or status changes that allow records about the same child to be linked over time and profiled within the system context.
assumptions: Assumes the returned history contains multiple observations or events about the same child rather than a single isolated datum.

title: Child history may reveal the child's identity through revealing attributes
description: Even if the flow is intended for an authorized parent, the retrieved child history may include revealing attributes such as age, milestones, incidents, or contextual details that make the child directly or indirectly identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes the history contains personal details about a specific child rather than fully aggregated or anonymized information.

title: Returned child history can serve as attributable evidence about the child
description: The delivered history may create a record that can later be used as evidence about the child's past states, events, or actions, reducing deniability regarding those facts.
assumptions: Assumes the history is stored, displayed, or otherwise retained in a way that preserves attribution to the child.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is somewhat context-dependent here because the flow description does not specify signatures, audit logs, or evidentiary use.

title: System response reveals existence of child history to the parent
description: The fact that the system returns child history to the parent reveals that such records exist for the child, and potentially that certain monitored events or categories of information are present.
assumptions: Assumes the presence, absence, or structure of the response can be observed by the parent and may disclose existence of underlying records.

title: Child history may be disclosed at finer granularity than necessary for parent review
description: Providing full child history to the parent may expose more detailed personal data than is strictly necessary for the review purpose, such as exact timestamps, detailed event narratives, or sensitive categories of history.
assumptions: Assumes the review purpose could be met with summarized or filtered history rather than complete detailed records.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify the exact fields returned, so the excess granularity risk is inferred from 'child history'.

title: Child may be unaware that their history is disclosed to the parent for review
description: The data subject is the child, but the flow sends the child's history to the parent. The child may not be aware that their personal history is being retrieved, reviewed, or disclosed in this way.
assumptions: Assumes the child is a distinct data subject and is not directly informed in the interaction.

title: Potential violation of data minimization in parent-facing child history retrieval
description: If the process returns more child-history data than is necessary for the parent's review purpose, the flow may violate the data minimization principle.
assumptions: Assumes the implementation may provide complete or overly detailed history instead of the minimum necessary subset.
uncertainty_note: This is a conditional compliance threat because the lawful scope and minimum necessary dataset are not specified in the prompt.
